attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'unless' structure, the per-company threshold and the Q1 2028 deadline. The conditions array labels the consequent as the antecedent; the contract corrects this by treating the missed threshold as the antecedent. The language is firm ('need to', 'aren't going to'), so it is a scorable forecast.

contract.note: The contract tests each company separately, uses realized monthly revenue, and takes the latest deadline, 31 March 2028. That is a fair, ordinary reading. 'Support their compute commitments' needs interpretation about financing, which the contract flags.

evidence.note: Anthropic S-1 risk factor (26 Oct 2026) on uncertain compute forecasts. It says nothing about Q1 2028 revenue or whether the company can pay its obligations.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 31 March 2028, after the evaluation date. Nobody can yet know whether the antecedent (missing $10B a month) happened, and no conclusive early event is in the packet. The only item is context. The forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the either/or claim about current AI revenues and the 'hundreds of dollars a user' figure. It drops only the rhetorical tail about what customers might pay. The statement is heavily rhetorical but has a factual core about the present.

contract.note: The speaker named no period, cohort, duration or basis. The contract picks Q1 2026 and defines a subsidy as cost-to-serve above payment. That is a reasonable plain reading, but the result depends on choices the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: The Anthropic S-1 (Oct 2026) says free access costs money, but gives no amount per user. It covers a period after Q1 2026 and only one lab, so it cannot establish the claimed subsidy.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no matched cost and payment records for any group of users in the target period. Nothing establishes subsidies of hundreds of dollars per user, or that the either/or split covers all AI revenues. The only item is an unquantified risk-factor disclosure. The available evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post. The $174B projection is credited to Anthropic, but the claim that it is necessary is his.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the claim that $174B in annual revenue by 2029 is necessary to pay for the compute. 'Must' here asserts necessity, not a recommendation, so treating it as a firm conditional forecast is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading 'by 2029' as the end of 2029 and revenue as realized annual revenue is ordinary and fair. Proving necessity is demanding, but that is what 'must' asserts. The early-resolution rule is sensible.

evidence.note: Anthropic's April 2026 disclosure of Amazon investment shows outside financing is available. It does not show the commitments being paid or what revenue was reached in 2029.

reviews.rationale: The horizon runs to 31 December 2029. The packet has no record of payment of the commitments and no 2029 revenue, and the financing news alone cannot settle the claim under the early-resolution rule. It is too early to score.

attribution.note: The forecast is Zitron's own ('I do not believe it will be'). Anthropic's profitability claim is only reported, not endorsed.

semantics.note: 'By then' refers to 2029. 'I do not believe it will be' is a flat rejection, not a probability hedge, so it is a scorable forecast. The separate clause about current profitability is correctly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'profitable' as full-year, company-wide profit by the end of 2029 is an ordinary, fair reading in the context of annual projections. The speaker did not pick a profit measure, and the contract flags this.

evidence.note: ProShares summary of the S-1: Q2 2026 operating income of $974M. That is one quarter of operating profit, which does not meet the early-resolution rule of full-year profit. It bears more on the separate claim about current profitability.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 31 December 2029, after the evaluation date. One profitable quarter does not meet the contract's early-resolution rule, which requires a full year of company-wide profit. The forecast cannot be scored yet.
